See also: Camion and camión

English

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from French camion.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (UK) IPA(key): /ˈkamɪən/
  • Audio (Southern England):(file)

Noun

[edit]

camion (plural camions)

  1. A truck or wagon, especially one used to transport ordnance.
    • 1929, Ernest Hemingway, A Farewell to Arms, Folio Society, published 2008, page 12:
      There were small gray motor cars that passed going very fast; usually there was an officer on the seat with the driver and more officers in the back seat. They splashed more mud than the camions even […]

Anagrams

[edit]
  • Camino, MINOCA, Monica, anicom, anomic, conima, manioc

Dutch

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

Borrowed from French camion.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • IPA(key): /kaːmˈjɔn/, /ˌkaː.miˈɔn/
  • Audio:(file)
  • Hyphenation: ca‧mi‧on
  • Rhymes: -ɔn

Noun

[edit]

camion m (plural camions, diminutive camionnetje n)

  1. (Belgium) lorry; truck

Synonyms

[edit]
  • truck
  • vrachtauto
  • vrachtwagen

Related terms

[edit]
  • camionette

French

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

    Unknown origin, however, most likely early 19th century. Possibly from chemin (“way, route”), see Spanish camino, or from Latin chamūlcus (“chariot”), from Ancient Greek χᾰμουλκός (khămoulkós, “crane, windlass, or possibly other machine”), from χθών (khthṓn, “earth, ground”) +‎ ἑλκέω (helkéō, “to drag”).

    Pronunciation

    [edit]
    • IPA(key): /ka.mjɔ̃/
    • Audio:(file)
    • (Marseille, Switzerland) IPA(key): /ka.mi.jɔ̃/
    • (Toulouse) IPA(key): /ka.mi.ɔŋ/
    • Audio (France (Vosges)):(file)
    • Audio (France (Vosges)):(file)
    • Audio (France (Lyon)):(file)
    • Audio (France (Somain)):(file)
    • Rhymes: -jɔ̃
    • Hyphenation: ca‧mion

    Noun

    [edit]

    camion m (plural camions)

    1. lorry (UK); truck (US)

    Derived terms

    [edit]

    • camion de déménagement
    • camion plateau
    • camion poubelle
    • camionner
    • camionnette
    • camionneur
    • tombé du camion
